answer: You create by hand the objects that have an add form: super-channel (add super-channel-<name> carriers <value> carrier-mode <value>), flexo-group (add flexo-group-<name> carriers rate modulation-format group-id), otu (add otu-1-5-L1-1-OTU4-1 parent flexo-group-1-5-L1-1 time-slots 1), the low-order odu (add odu-<name> odu-type ODU4i/ODUflexi parent-odu ... time-slots ...), trib-ptp and xcon. The system creates optical-carrier, optical-channel and flexo (set/show only, no add), and the high order ODU is automatically created when an SCH is created. The stated pre-condition on odu is: Super-channel must be added before Low Order ODUs can be added. Check managed-by (system or user) on any facility; only user-created facilities can be user deleted, and odu class shows high-order, low-order or mapped.

The bit error rate test is the bert command (Operational Mode): bert start test-id=TestX resource=ethernet-1-6-T1 test-signal-type=scrambled-idles test-signal-monitoring-type=scrambled-idles test-signal-direction=ingress test-signal-monitoring-direction=ingress test-duration=10, then bert get, bert stop test-id=TestX (test-id mandatory for stop) and bert delete. test-signal-type is none, PRBS31, PRBS31NONINV or scrambled-idles; monitoring type adds fec-frames. test-duration min 10 s, max 1000 hrs, 0 means indefinite. You inject a test pattern per facility on odu-diagnostics-<name>/<direction>: test-signal-type none (default), PRBS31Q, PRBS13Q, scrambled-idles, PRBS9, PRBS31, PRBS31_NONINV; test-signal-direction ingress, egress or both (default ingress); test-signal-monitoring true/false (default false). Loop it back with the loopback attribute on otu, odu or optical-carrier: none (default), facility or terminal, with loopback-mode loopback or loopback-and-continue.

L1 encryption is carried by secure-entity, and both of its references are mandatory: add secure-entity-<name> supporting-facility <value> remote-secure-entity <value>. supporting-facility is the local facility being encrypted (optical-carrier on 1830 GX G40, odu on 1830 GX G30, OTUflex for CHM7/CHM7x L1 service encryption); remote-secure-entity is the AID of the matching far-end optical carrier, ODU or OTUFlex, so that facility must already exist at the other end. enabled defaults to false, so set enabled true. re-key-frequency is 3600..86400 s, default 28800; re-key-fail-policy kill-traffic or continue-traffic (default continue-traffic); traffic-kill-offset 0..86400 s, default 0; alarm-report-control defaults to inhibited. Underneath, IKEv2 must be up: an ikev2-local-instance with scope data-path-encryption on a card whose host-card-encryption-capability is yes, plus an ikev2-peer with destination set to the far end and authentication-scheme x.509-certificate (default, requiring local-certificate and peer-certificate) or pre-shared-key.

The telemetry object configures persistent and dynamic telemetry (show telemetry, set telemetry id <string>, string 0..4096); it is system-managed and cannot be manually deleted. show subscriptions lists what is currently subscribed. For one of them, show current-subscription-<subscription-name> gives related-session-id, related-dial-out-server, session-type (gnmi-dial-in, gnmi-dial-out-tunnel, gnmi-dial-out-reverse-rpc), session-protocol gnmi, encoding json, bytes, proto, ascii or json-ietf (default json-ietf), transfer-mode stream (default), once or poll, updates-only (default false) and user-access. What each one watches comes from show subscription-path-<subscription-name>/<subscription-path-name>: subscription-path (1..520), subscription-path-origin, subscription-path-mode target-defined (default), on-change or sample, sample-interval and heartbeat-interval in ms (both default 0), suppress-redundant (default true).

The database is encrypted at rest. show db-protection-scheme reports encryption-algorithm xts-aes-256-plain64 (AES-256 in XTS mode, 64-byte block), integrity-algorithm hmac-sha2-512 or none, integrity-status passed-on-bootup, failed-on-bootup or disabled, and mode encryption-only or encryption-with-integrity, which is changed via the db-migrate RPC. Before you can take a copy the db-passphrase must be configured: take-snapshot is only accepted if it is set globally (set security-policies db-passphrase) or supplied inline (take-snapshot db-passphrase=***). It needs a minimum of 40 characters (security-policies length 40..200), no dictionary words, special characters per the 85-character Z85 set; automatic DB snapshots are not enabled until it is set. take-snapshot [db-instance=] takes temp (default), manual, onehour, oneday, oneweek or rollback, plus an optional description (0..128). Snapshots are listed with show database.

Start with show route-<rib-name>/<destination-prefix> [special-next-hop] [source-protocol]. It lists system routes from all sources; source-protocol says whether the entry came from OSPF, BGP or static, and special-next-hop is none, blackhole or unreachable (for blackhole and unreachable routes no next-hop is created under the route). Then confirm resolution with show next-hop-<rib-name>/<destination-prefix>/<interface> [next-hop-address], for example show next-hop-IPv4/0.0.0.0/0/DCN. The instance it landed in is the RIB: show rib-<rib-name> [vrf] [address-family]. All routes in a RIB belong to the same address family, ipv4-unicast or ipv6-unicast, the vrf leaf gives the VRF the RIB is bound to, and for each routing instance the system provides one system-controlled default RIB per supported address family. show vrf-<name> [type] [chassis-name] [description] shows the VRF, type mgmt or internal.

The rejection comes from security-policies. strict-password-check (default true) requires minimum length 8, at least one lower case letter, one upper case letter, one number and one symbol, and the user name may not be part of the password; disabled leaves only a minimum length of 1. minimum-password-length is separately configurable, range 1..200, default 8. enforce-password-history-check (default true) blocks reuse of the previous 5 passwords, with password-history-size range 1..200, default 5. These only affect newly defined passwords. The lockout is per user: max-invalid-login, consecutive invalid logins before suspension, range 0..255, default 5; suspension-time, range 0..1440 minutes, default 5. show user-<name> gives user-status (lockout) and failed-logins, which resets on a successful login. To clear the stuck session, list them with show session and run kill-session <session-id>, where session-id is <ip-address>:<port> and cannot be your own session.

Untouched syslog defaults: remote-logging-switch true, source-address localhost, log-file-message-coalescence true, log-relay false, assignment-method both, niap-compliant-logging false, privacy-mode false. On log-file, number-of-files is the maximum retained, range 1..20, default 10; when rotating because max-file-size is reached the oldest files beyond that count are discarded. max-file-size is 1..30 megabytes, default 30. source-facilities defaults to all and severity is informational and above by default; sensitive-data is none for a regular log file. The default system log file cannot be edited or deleted. Console logging is off by default (log-console enabled false). Remote collectors default to port 514, transport udp, message-format rfc5424, enabled true, origin manual. The single switch that turns off everything remote is set syslog remote-logging-switch false, which disables all remote logging destinations.

What is raised now: show current-alarms, which reports number-of-alarms and last-changed (timestamp of the last raise or clear); show alarms and show alarm-<alarm-id> give detail such as perceived-severity, service-affecting, reported-time, corrective-action and operator-state. Most alarms have both automatic raise and clear criteria. The small subset with no clear criteria is cleared by hand with clear [-f] alarm [alarm-type=]<value> [[resource=]<value>], for example clear alarm DBRESTOREFAIL; find them with show alarm-inventory can-be-cleared-by-user=true. That applies only to system-wide alarms not associated with a particular resource. Operator state is set with set-alarm-state [state=]<value> [[acknowledge-text=]<value>] (all-alarms | alarm-id-list=..., 1 to 10 ids), states none, ack, close. Whether inhibiting reporting drops alarms already up is decided by alarm-control arc-behavior: leave-alarms (default) leaves them raised, clear-alarms clears them when ARC is set to inhibit.

Temperature comes from real-time PM: show pm gives a per-resource real-time table with instant, avg, min and max, including temperature (C) for a line card such as card-1-1 and for card-1-FANCTRL-1, temperature plus input-current/input-power/input-voltage for each card-1-PEM-n, inlet-temperature (C) and actual-power-draw (W) for chassis-1, and fan-speed (percent) per card-1-FAN-n. Narrow it with the pm-filter fields AID, resource, resource-type, data-type or parameter, for example show pm card-1-7; -i=<chassis-name> scopes to one chassis, -t gives a standard table, -n= caps records (default 1000). show pm-resource-<resource> gives real-time-supervision and real-time-data-last-reset. Physically the state shows on the LEDs: show leds or show led status, with entries like led-1-1/fault, led-1-1/power and led-1-2/chassis-critical, status off, green, flashing-green, yellow, amber, red, flashing-red, cycling or not-available. show slot and card avail-state also reflect it.

The line is the ots facility. show ots-<name> gives span-loss-derived-rx and span-loss-derived-tx, the measured span loss based on OSC powers including losses external to the fiber, 0..99 dB where 99 dB means OLOS; span-loss-transmit and span-loss-receive, the configured fiber loss, 0..80 dB (receive also allows 99, default 0, and changing it is traffic affecting); span-loss-reference measured (default) or configured; span-loss-alarm-threshold, autonomously set and persistent, default 99 dB, refreshable with the update command in measured mode; span-loss-aging-margin-rx 0.00..10.00 dB, default 1.0; external-attenuation-tx/rx 0..30 dB; fiber-type (default SSMF) and fiber-length-derived-rx/tx. The amplifier shows the compensation: gain-operating and gain-target 0..40 dB, gain-range-actual, gain-adjustment -20.00..20.00, optimum-edfa-gain, input-power-mon and output-power-mon -99.00..99.00 dBm, tilt-actual and tilt-target -5..5 dB, control-mode auto-max-pw (default) or manual, span-loss-control enabled by default, control-state converged, fine-tuning, adjusting or stopped.

Going down: trib-ptp, the tributary client physical termination between the transceiver (TOM) and the client protocol, with service-type such as 100GBE, 400GBE or OTU4; the client protocol layer (ethernet, or a client otu); the low order odu (ODU4i, ODUflexi, ODU4, ODUflex) with trib-port-number and time-slots; the xcon, the Layer 1 digital service joining source and destination, direction two-way; the high order ODU (class high-order, ODUCn/ODUCni), created automatically when the SCH is created; then otu and flexo-group (carriers, rate, modulation-format, group-id) with the per-interface flexo (foic-type foic1.2 to foic4.16, fec-type default ofec); then optical-carrier, grouped by super-channel, and line-ptp. The handover from digital to optical is at optical-carrier: it is the object holding frequency, actual-frequency, wavelength, tx-power, baud-rate, modulation-format, grid-spacing and spectral-bandwidth, and it is bound upward by the carriers attribute of flexo-group and super-channel. Walk the chain with supporting-facilities and supported-facilities.

No, they are two different objects. A counter limit is a PM threshold: add or set pm-threshold-<resource>/<period>/<direction>/<location>/<parameter> [low-threshold <value>] [high-threshold <value>]; values are uint64, int64 or decimal64, or na, or not-supported, default na; direction ingress, egress, all or na (default all); location all, na, near-end or far-end (default all). The crossing is only reported if tca-supervision is true on the matching pm-control-entry, or default-tca-supervision on pm-profile-entry for newly created resources. System defaults and the permitted range come from show pm-threshold-profile-... [default-low-threshold] [default-high-threshold] [min-value] [max-value]. Changing how loudly an existing fault is reported is instead set alarm-severity-entry-<resource-type>/<alarm-type>/<direction>/<location> severity <value>, or set alarm-severity-profile <profile-entry> severity <value>, with severity critical, event, major, minor, not-reported or warning. Both alarm severity objects are system-managed and cannot be manually deleted.

Stop the reporting with alarm-report-control on the card: set card-<name> alarm-report-control inhibited (values allowed, inhibited). The same attribute exists on the facilities the card hosts (trib-ptp, otu, odu, flexo, optical-carrier, ots, amplifier, line-ptp), where the default is allowed, so inhibit those too for silence at facility level. You can also use set card-<name> admin-state maintenance (admin-state lock, unlock, maintenance). What happens to alarms already raised is not decided on the card: it is the system-wide switch set alarm-control arc-behavior. leave-alarms, the default, leaves current alarms raised when ARC is set to inhibit; clear-alarms clears them. The companion alarm-control alarm-soaking-behavior is automatic (soaking time from the FM profile) by default, or no-soak. Verify with show alarm-control and show current-alarms.

A secure application uses an X509v3 certificate as its digital identity. show secure-application-<id> [type] [active-certificate-id] [in-use] [status] [verify-client-cert] tells you which one it presents: active-certificate-id is the assigned list (string 0..128, for example set secure-application-gRPC active-certificate-id certX,certY) and in-use is the leafref to active-certificate-id, the certificate actually in use. type is server or client, status enabled or disabled, verify-client-cert disabled (default) or required, where required is what TLS mutual authentication needs and only affects new connections. Before it comes up, import the end-entity certificate and its CA chain: import-certificate local-certificate certificate-name=local-cert-1 <PEM string> <passphrase> and import-certificate trusted-certificate certificate-name=trusted-cert-1 <PEM string>, adding -i to pull intermediates out of a bundle; root certificates must be installed individually. Then check show local-certificate-<id> status (valid, pending-import, expired, revoked, untrusted, future), trust-chain and used-by.

Pipe the show pm output through the CSV display filter: show pm <command flag> | display csv, which produces CSV importable to a spreadsheet such as Excel; display xml and display json are also available. Restrict it to the 15-minute bins with the pm-filter fields, for example show pm pm-15min, and add AID, parameter, resource, resource-type or data-type filters to narrow further (use show pm <tab> for the complete list of supported filters). Bin 0 is the current data and bins 1 to n are history; select a range with -sbin=<number> and -ebin=<number>, or a time window with -st=<timestamp> and -et=<timestamp> in the form 2021-02-01T10:00:00+01:00. Other flags: -t forces the standard single generic table format, -n=<number-of-records> caps records per chassis (default 1000), -s=<skip-records> pages through the data, and -i=<chassis-name> scopes to one chassis (only once per command).

Look it up in the PM catalog with show pm-catalog <string>, where string is the catalog name. For example show pm-catalog parameter-undersized returns pm-parameter-undersized with units packets and type counter. The equivalent per-parameter view is show pm-parameter-<parameter> [units] [type], for instance show pm-parameter-severely-errored-seconds, and show pm-parameter on its own lists all PM parameters. units is drawn from na, dBm, ms, ps, ps/nm, dB, seconds, packets, events, octets, bits, blocks, times, percent, bit-ratio, C, frames, W, V, A, rpm, ps2, mA, words, cw, nm, bytes, errors and MHz; type is counter or gauge. Both commands are available in Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode.

Turn off data supervision for that resource with set pm-control <entity> data-supervision <true|false>, for example set pm-control pm-resource-card-1-1 data-supervision false. data-supervision is the real-time data supervision flag for the resource; its values are true and false and the default is true. show pm-control lists the currently existing resources in the system that support PM data. The equivalent per-instance control is set pm-resource-<resource> real-time-supervision false (true/false, default true), and show pm-resource-<resource> reports real-time-supervision along with resource-type, AID and real-time-data-last-reset. Both are available in Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode. Note that global-data-supervision on pm-profile must be left at manual for per-resource control to apply, since auto-enabled globally enables PM data-supervision.

Yes. pm-control-entry is exactly that scope: one resource, one period, one direction, one location. Run set pm-control-entry-<resource>/pm-15min/ingress/near-end tca-supervision true. The key fields are resource (Instance ID), period (PM period, e.g. pm-15min or pm-24h), direction ingress, egress, all or na (default all) and location all, na, near-end or far-end (default all). The same entry carries data-supervision (true/false) if you want to separate data collection from threshold crossing supervision. show pm-control-entry-<resource>/<period>/<direction>/<location> [supported-parameters] [data-supervision] [tca-supervision] reads it back, where supported-parameters is the list of PM parameters that resource type supports for that direction and location, with a maximum of 100 elements. Access is Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode.

Use show pm-parameter-<parameter> [units] [type]. The type attribute is the answer to counter versus gauge: its only values are counter and gauge. units gives the reported unit, taken from na, dBm, ms, ps, ps/nm, dB, seconds, packets, events, octets, bits, blocks, times, percent, bit-ratio, C, frames, W, V, A, rpm, ps2, mA, words, cw, nm, bytes, errors and MHz. Example: show pm-parameter pm-parameter-undersized returns units packets and type counter. show pm-parameter on its own lists all PM parameters, and show pm-parameter-severely-errored-seconds targets one by name. The same information is in the catalog via show pm-catalog <catalog-name>. Available in Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode.

Yes, through the pm-profile object, which holds all resources that support PM data together with their related default configuration. Run set pm-profile global-data-supervision auto-enabled. The attribute takes auto-enabled or manual and defaults to manual. auto-enabled is the global enabling of the PM data-supervision flag, so you do not have to toggle it individually; manual means the flag is controlled via pm-profile-entry, or directly per pm-control-entry. Read it back with show pm-profile. The pm-profile object is managed by the system and cannot be manually deleted. Access mode is Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode.

Set the per-resource-type defaults on pm-profile-entry: set pm-profile-entry-<resource-type>/<direction>/<location>/<period> default-data-supervision true. default-data-supervision controls, for newly created resources of this type, whether they have PM data supervision automatically enabled; the companion default-tca-supervision does the same for threshold crossing supervision. Both take true or false. The key fields are resource-type (Instance ID), direction ingress, egress, all or na (default all), location all, na, near-end or far-end (default all), and period (PM period such as pm-15min or pm-24h). Read it back with show pm-profile-entry-<resource-type>/<direction>/<location>/<period> [default-data-supervision] [default-tca-supervision]. This is per resource type; existing instances are still controlled by pm-control-entry, and pm-profile global-data-supervision must stay at manual for these entries to govern.

Read real-time-data-last-reset on the resource: show pm-resource-<resource> [resource-type] [AID] [real-time-supervision] [real-time-data-last-reset], for example show pm-resource-trib-ptp-1-7-T9. real-time-data-last-reset is the date and time of the last real-time data reset for that resource; if the data was never reset, it is the date and time of the resource's creation. The same output gives resource-type, AID (string, length 1..64) and real-time-supervision (true/false, default true), plus the pm-control-entry children such as pm-control-entry-trib-ptp-1-7-T9/pm-15min/ingress/near-end. The counters themselves are cleared with clear pm real-time, optionally narrowed by resource, resource-type, AID, direction, location or period. Access mode is Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode.

Create a pm-threshold on that instance: add pm-threshold-<resource>/<period>/<direction>/<location>/errored-seconds high-threshold <value>, then use set to change it, show to read it and delete pm-threshold-<resource>/<period>/<direction>/<location>/<parameter> to remove it. resource is an Instance ID, period is the PM period (for example pm-15min or pm-24h), direction is ingress, egress, all or na (default all) and location is all, na, near-end or far-end (default all). high-threshold and low-threshold accept a Number (uint64, int64 or decimal64), or na for not applicable, or not-supported; the default is na. Access mode is Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode. For the crossing to be reported, tca-supervision must be true on the matching pm-control-entry-<resource>/<period>/<direction>/<location>.

The pm-threshold-profile object holds the PM configuration per parameter for a resource type. Run show pm-threshold-profile-<resource-type>/<direction>/<location>/<period>/<parameter> [low-threshold] [high-threshold] [default-low-threshold] [default-high-threshold] [min-value] [max-value]. default-low-threshold and default-high-threshold are the system defined default values for that parameter, and min-value and max-value are the minimum and maximum values allowed for it; all four are show-only. low-threshold and high-threshold are the configured values and can be set. All of them accept a Number (uint64, int64 or decimal64), or na, or not-supported. direction is ingress, egress, all or na (default all) and location is all, na, near-end or far-end (default all). Example: set pm-threshold-profile-OTUC14i/ingress/near-end/pm-24h/errored-seconds high-threshold 1200.
